But in the way in which he is seen as he is, he is perhaps now seen by the angels; by us he will be seen then, when we shall be equal to the angels. But not even then will he be seen as these visible things which are discerned by bodily sight, but “the only begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, he will declare him,” which pertains not to the eyes but to the sight of the mind. He said above that through charity the first coming of the Son of God into the world was made for the salvation of the world; here through the same charity he announces the salvation of the faithful at the second coming, on the day of judgment. While he commends love, he neither wholly passes over the love of God in silence, nor names it often; the love of the enemy he passes over entirely in silence; fraternal charity he mentions most frequently. Why is this? Since he says it is no great thing if we love those who love us, unless love reaches even to enemies? But he who has come to the love of enemies will not pass over the brethren. For it is fitting that, like fire, it should first seize what is nearest, and so descend to what is farther off. He who wishes of an enemy that he become a brother loves a brother. For he does not love in him what he is, but what he wishes him to be; as a craftsman loves wood cut from the forest, of which he is going to make something: he does not love what it is, but what he is going to make. He has therefore admonished no less concerning charity. In mutual love is the perfection of divine charity.

79_marg1468: The Spirit. That is, the human soul, which he gave up in the passion. The water and blood which flowed from his side, which could not have happened if he had not had the true nature of flesh. But even before the passion “his sweat became as drops of blood”, showing the truth of the flesh. Moreover, that from the side of one already dead, against nature, water and blood flowed living, bore witness that the body of the Lord would after death live better, and that his death would give us life. And that the sweat flowed upon the earth like blood signified that with his blood he would wash the Church throughout the whole world.
79_interl4036: one God, bearing witness of the same thing
79_marg1469: By this it appears that Jesus is the truth, true God, true man, concerning both of whom we have certain testimony: concerning the divinity through the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit; concerning the humanity through the soul, the water, and the blood. The Father gave testimony of the divinity when he says: “This is my beloved Son.” The Son himself gave it when he was transfigured on the mountain and showed both the power of divinity and the hope of eternal blessedness. The Holy Spirit gave it when he rested upon him baptized in the form of a dove, or when at the calling of the name of Christ he filled the hearts of believers.
79_interl4037: and because we have such certain testimonies, therefore we ought to accept these, since we are accustomed to accept even the testimonies of men, who can lie.
79_marg1470: Great is the testimony of David, a man, which he bears of the Son of God: “The Lord said to my Lord, Sit on my right hand”; who also brings in the Son speaking: “The Lord said to me, Thou art my Son.” Greater the testimony of the forerunner, who says: “I baptize you with water; he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.” But greater is the testimony of the Father, who sent visibly upon him the Spirit with whom he was always filled; as if he said: if you believe men announcing the coming beforehand, believe the Father testifying that Christ has come.
79_interl4041: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
79_marg1471: He understands the Father as true in the testimony of the Son; he who does not believe says the Father is a liar. Therefore the Jews say in vain that they believe in the Father, while they despise Christ.
79_marg1472: Because the Father testifies of the Son, let us believe in the Son; for he who believes in the Son, so that by working well he tends toward the Son himself, has the testimony of God in himself, as though God also testified of him that he, believing thus, will be in the number of the sons of God, the Son himself promising this to his own: “If any man minister to me, him will my Father honour.” If therefore you have God as witness of your faith, what does the disgrace or persecution of men hurt you? “If God be for us, who is against us?”
79_interl4043: says that he is not the Son, or less than the Father
79_interl4047: “Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased”; and in the passion: “I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.”
79_marg1473: He testified of the Son, and also of us, the adopted sons, that through his only Son he would give us eternal life, now in hope, and at last in reality.
79_marg1474: In faith and confession of his name, in the reception of his sacraments, because “no man cometh to the Father but by me,” and: “There is no other name by which we must be saved.” And lest it seem he had said little in saying that life is in the Son, he adds that the Son himself is that life. For as the Father hath life in himself, so he hath given the Son also to have life in himself, who gives his own eternal life.

79_interl4052: lest you be deceived by the frauds of those who deny that Christ is the Son of God, because by the merit of faith you will have life.
79_interl4053: and you must hope for heavenly goods not only in the future, from the faith of Christ; but also in this life there is confidence that we shall obtain whatever we have asked for salutarily.
79_marg1475: He impresses again in many ways what he had promised above, so that he may rouse us to pray more eagerly.
79_marg1476: That we may ask what he wills, or come to ask being such as he desires us to be. If we desire our salvation and that of our neighbours, let us not be at odds with the will of God. If our will through ignorance departs from the will of God, the good will of God corrects our foolish one, as happened to the apostle Paul.
79_marg1477: Not according to our carnal desires, for we know not what we should pray for as we ought, unless he himself shows his will, who understands our advantage better than we ourselves do.
79_marg1478: We obtain it as when we ask for a brother, for whom we must ask.

79_interl4055: and not only in future time will he hear, but we also know that he has heard and hears us daily. And by this, that we are heard now, we are certain of the future.
79_interl4056: and not only in future time, giving effect to the petition
79_marg1479: We know that, etc. Because we know that we have from him the petitions we ask, let us ask for nothing adverse to him; nothing but what he has taught us, what he has inspired in us to ask for. Even if we err in something, we are at once corrected.
79_interl4057: by confession, or even in another way
79_interl4058: not criminally, or not unto death
79_marg1480: He speaks of daily and light sins, which, as they are hard to avoid, so are easily cured. If you have sinned in word or thought, or by forgetfulness or ignorance, confess to your brother, as James teaches: ask that he intercede for you. And if he in turn confesses to you, do you also intercede for him. Here the Lord’s prayer suffices, and mutual confession is a light penance. But if the sin is grave, bring in the priests of the Church and be corrected by their examination.
79_interl4062: to him who sins, I say
79_marg1481: That which separates from God, as death separates the soul from the body.
79_marg1482: The Lord commands us to pray for persecutors; here he says we are not to pray for certain men, because there are sins among brethren that are graver than the persecution of enemies. A brother’s sin is unto death when, after the knowledge of God which was given through grace, someone attacks the brotherhood and, having been reconciled, is driven against grace by the firebrands of envy. There is a sin not unto death: if someone has not withdrawn his love from his brother, but through some weakness of mind has not performed the duties of brotherhood. Whence Christ: “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” For they had not yet been made sharers through the grace of the Spirit and entered the fellowship of holy brotherhood. So also Stephen prayed for those who had not received the grace of God. Paul does not pray for Alexander, because, when he was already a brother, he assailed the brotherhood. He prays for those who had given way through fear. Whence: “All have forsaken me,” but “may it not be laid to their charge.”
79_interl4066: Because what is not corrected in this life, pardon for it after death is asked in vain; and this can be understood of every criminal sin; whatever differs from the rule of equity is numbered among sins; but the smallest do not harm the just, while some so differ from all justice that, unless they are corrected, they plunge into punishment.
79_marg1483: All, as it were: we must truly pray for those who sin not unto death, because all are occupied with many sins, and no one can be without sin, because “all iniquity is sin.” But above, there is another, a sin unto death, which is not committed through human frailty, and therefore is not purged by the prayer of the just, since “they who do such things shall not obtain the kingdom of God.”
79_interl4067: who has the seed of God in him cannot sin unto death; for at the same time he cannot work righteousness and sin.
79_marg1484: He who is born of God does not sin unto death; he who is not born sins. But we are of those who are born of God, therefore we will not sin, we will not be touched by the enemy; but the lovers of the world are subject to the malign enemy.
79_marg1485: David sinned grievously, but because he was born of God, he belonged to the fellowship of the sons of God; he did not sin unto death but by repenting merited pardon.
79_interl4069: the grace by which they are reborn, according to the purpose by which the saints are called, keeps them from committing sin unto death, though in whatever things they have fallen through human frailty, it defends them that they may not be touched by the malign enemy.
79_marg1486: Because a man is the son of God voluntarily and not by nature, the text fittingly added one of this kind:
79_marg1487: Those who persevere in the generation of God cannot sin, nor be touched by the evil one. As day and night cannot be mixed, so righteousness and iniquity, the malign one and the generation of God, touch. Therefore the malign one sits and afflicts some, but not to their harm.
79_marg1488: Not only the lovers of the world, but also the recently born, who have no discernment of good and evil, belong through the first prevarication to the kingdom of the devil, unless by the grace of God they are plucked from darkness.
79_interl4071: through the flesh, not except on account of our salvation
79_marg1489: No one can come to eternal life without divine knowledge, no one can know without the grace of God, because: “No one knoweth the Son, but the Father: neither doth any one know the Father, but the Son, and he to whom it shall please the Son to reveal him.” For the Son reveals both the Father and the Son, appearing visible in the flesh, and he made known to the world the secrets of the divinity through the gospel.
79_interl4073: by believing the true Son of God
79_interl4076: by this we shall be God’s, living in God without end, in the living one without beginning or end
79_marg1490: And because you know the true God and true man and await eternal life, keep yourselves from the teachings of heretics, who take on themselves the appearance of holiness, who by perverse doctrines change the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of corruptible things; for covetousness is the service of idols; and those who even set the world before God are idolaters.
79_marg1491: Although he has given them testimony of perfection in many things, yet it may be feared lest someone recently converted has kept the remnants of superstition in mind.
